name: Rollout stability for rectified-flow 2D video forecaster

description: BASELINE: decoupled Gaussian pixel-noise context aug (TECHNIQUE=pixnoise, SIGMA=0.4). Reproduces user's finding: pixel noise fails on structured image data — sharpness_ratio=0.27 (very blurry, ideal 1.0), mass_drift=0.59. This is the bar to beat.

asi.hypothesis: Pixel-noise context aug is the known-weak baseline for image data; should reproduce blur/mass-drift failure
asi.setup: 2D video, IMG=32, C=1, K=2 ctx, Lorenz-driven blob, RF x-pred 1/(1-t)^2 weighted, 2000 train steps
asi.finding: Confirmed: pixnoise mmd=0.40, sharpness 0.27 (blurry), mass_drift 0.59. Noise floor mmd_floor~3e-4 (healthy). 64s/run.
asi.next: Try blur (known to help per user) — should beat this and validate benchmark

name: Rollout stability for rectified-flow 2D video forecaster (energy distance)

description: BASELINE (re-metric): pixnoise, now measured with energy distance (non-saturating). rollout_ed=9770, ed_late=15570. Metric switched because Gaussian-kernel MMD saturated identically at 0.404 for both pixnoise and blur.

asi.finding: Switched primary metric from Gaussian-kernel MMD (saturated at 0.404 for both pixnoise and blur — k_ab->0, mbb->1 ceiling) to ENERGY DISTANCE which is non-saturating. pixnoise ED=9770, ed_late=15570 (late drifts worse - good temporal signal), ed_floor=0 (healthy). huge dynamic range now.
asi.metric_history: MMD saturated identically (0.404124) for pixnoise AND blur -> useless. Energy distance fixes this.
asi.next: Run blur to confirm metric now discriminates (should differ from pixnoise). Then iterate techniques.

description: blur context aug BLUR_SIGMA=0.8: ED 9770->5214 (-47%), ed_late 15570->6240. Reproduces user finding that blur beats pixel noise. Cost: train_loss 0.16->3.37 (blur degrades condition), sharpness 1.65 (slight artifacts).

asi.finding: Blur(0.8) ED=5214 vs pixnoise 9770 (-47%). ed_late 6240 vs 15570. Confirms benchmark reproduces user's real-world finding: blur >> pixel noise for image rollout stability. BUT sharpness=1.65 (>1=artifacty) and train_loss=3.37 (blur degrades condition, harder to learn dynamics). Tradeoff: stability up, precision down + slight artifacts.
asi.next: Try smaller blur sigma (0.5) for better dynamics learning; then novel techniques (selffeed scheduled sampling, manifold_noise) to beat blur without the artifact/precision cost

description: selffeed (scheduled sampling, prob=0.3) + mild blur 0.4: ED 5214->725 (7x better than blur, 13x vs pixnoise). sharpness 0.88 (ideal!), mass_drift 0.08, train_loss 0.12 (low). Fixes blur's artifacts+precision loss. The principled exposure-bias fix wins decisively.

asi.finding: BREAKTHROUGH: selffeed (scheduled sampling) ED=725 vs blur 5214 (7x) vs pixnoise 9770 (13x). sharpness 0.88 (near ideal 1.0!), mass_drift 0.08, train_loss 0.12 (lower than pixnoise - model learns dynamics fine since mostly real data). Fixes ALL of blur's problems (artifacts 1.65, precision loss 3.37). This is THE technique for rollout stability.
asi.mechanism: Feeds model its own 1-step predictions as context during training (prob 0.3) + mild blur 0.4 -> directly closes train/inference gap. Principled exposure-bias fix.
asi.cost: wall 168s vs 65s (2.6x) due to extra sampling in train loop
asi.next: Tune selffeed prob; try pure selffeed without blur; test deeper rollout stability

description: DISCARD: pure selffeed (no blur). ED 725->1200, ed_late 906->2988. Mild blur on self-fed context is needed — smooths model errors.

asi.finding: Pure selffeed (no blur) WORSE: ED 725->1200, ed_late 906->2988. The mild blur (0.4) on self-fed predictions is important - it smooths model errors giving cleaner degraded contexts. Combo selffeed+mild-blur is the winner, not pure scheduled sampling.
asi.next: Tune selffeed prob up (0.5); maybe multi-step selffeed (2-step predictions) for deeper exposure

description: DISCARD: selffeed prob=0.5 too aggressive. ED 725->5869, ed_late 906->15739 (late divergence).

asi.finding: selffeed prob=0.5 MUCH worse: ED 725->5869, ed_late 906->15739 (diverges late, near pixnoise level). Too much self-feeding on early bad predictions harms dynamics learning. Sharp phase transition around prob 0.3-0.5. sharpness/mass still ok (0.83/0.09) but late rollout explodes -> compounding error sensitivity.
asi.next: Try prob=0.2 (less aggressive). Note: high run-to-run variance in ed_late due to chaotic rollout amplification - may need multi-seed confirmation of best config.

description: DISCARD: selffeed prob=0.2 ED=1410 (worse than 0.3). Optimum near 0.3.

asi.finding: selffeed prob=0.2 ED=1410 (worse than 0.3's 725). Bracket: 0.2->1410, 0.3->725, 0.5->5869. Optimum near 0.3. But single-run variance on chaotic rollout is high - need to confirm 0.3 reproduces.
asi.next: Re-run prob=0.3 to confirm 725 reproduces (not noise)

description: CONFIRM (discard dup): selffeed prob=0.3 reproduces ED=773 (vs 725 first). Robust.

asi.finding: CONFIRMED reproducible: selffeed prob=0.3 re-run ED=773 (first run 725), ed_late=1327. Robust ~7x better than blur. sharpness 0.78, mass_drift 0.14. Technique is real, not noise.
asi.next: Implement 2-step compounded selffeed (selffeed2) to expose deeper rollout errors

description: DISCARD: selffeed2 (2-step compounded) ED=988 (worse than 1-step 725), 280s wall. 1-step self-feed sufficient.

asi.finding: selffeed2 (2-step compounded) ED=988 WORSE than 1-step selffeed 725, ed_late 1695, and 280s wall (1.6x slower). Deeper compounding doesn't help - 1-step exposure is sufficient, compounded context is noisier. Optimum is single-step scheduled sampling.
asi.next: Try manifold_noise (cheap on-manifold perturbation); then write up findings
